# General Workflow

This chapter provides a three-part walkthrough of the City Scan repo for new users. The diagram below illustrates the general workflow of performing a standard City Scan. 

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A(Setup) --> B(Configuring inputs)
  B --> C{Running Scan}
  C --> J(scan --collect)
  J --> K(scan --analyze)
  C --> D(scan --all)
  C --> E(scan --parallel)
  D --> F(scan --multianalysis)
  E --> F
  K --> F
  F --> G(scan --render maps)
  F --> H(scan --render charts)
  F --> I(scan --render scan-calculations)
```

## Part 1. Basic Setup
::: {.callout-note}
See [Part 4. Getting Started/ Setup Instructions](setting-up.qmd) for full details of prerequisites and installations
:::

City Scan uses multiple programming languages and software to run, including Git, Python, R, Quarto, and Google Cloud. The steps required for setups are below:

- Clone the repo  `https://github.com/cityresilience/city-scan`
- Create conda env + activate cityscan 
- Installing City Scan as Python Package via `pip install -e .` for the scan CLI 
- GCS and GEE authentication via `gcloud auth application-default login` 
- Install Quarto 
- Run `scan --check` to verify everything passes 

## Part 2. Configuring Inputs
Inputs folder is where you can specify your area of interests (AOI), types of analysis to conduct, and certain global analysis parameters. 

- Drop AOI shapefile into `inputs/AOI/`
- Edit `inputs/city_inputs.yml` 
- Edit `inputs/menu.yml` 

## Part 3. Running a Scan

When running a scan, we are essentially going through several phases. The general flow is collect → analyze → multianalysis → render. 

1. [**Collect**](running-first-cityscan.qmd) stage is retrieveing specified datasets as indicated in inputs configuration from various publicly available sources for the specified AOI. As an output, you will retrieve TIFFs, GeoJSONs, or Geopackages in your output folder. 

    To conduct **collect** stage, run in your terminal

    ```zsh
    scan --collect
    ```
2. [**Analyze**](running-first-cityscan.qmd) stage is conducting various analysis on a single task, such as seeing the statistical distribution, applying threshold, extracting median/mean values, etc. As an output, you will retrieve various CSVs in your output folder. 

     To conduct **analyze** stage, run in your terminal

    ```zsh
    scan --analyze
    ```
3. Alternatively, you can **batch data collection and data analysis together by looping over tasks** by running: 
    
    ```zsh
    scan --all
    ```
    
    Or, you can leverage your computer memory and **parallelizing data collection and data analysis together per tasks** by running: 
    
    ```zsh
    scan --all --parallel
    ```

::: {.callout-warning}
[**Internal Note**] Perhaps in the future, `scan --all` and `scan --all --parallel` should be reserved to orchestrate the whole process, including multianalysis, render, and scan-calculations
:::

4. [**Multianalysis**](running-first-cityscan.qmd) stage is performing cross-task analysis after single tasks analysis have been executed. For example, this stage executes analysis of flood-exposed population, which requires both flood analysis and population analysis to have been conducted. To do this, run in your terminal: 

    ```zsh
    scan --multianalysis
    ```

5. [**Render**](running-first-cityscan.qmd) stage is generating various visualizations as results of previous stages. This includes rendering maps and charts as PNGs or HTMLs. 

    ```zsh
    # Static maps — applies styling from source/layers.yml, writes PNGs to 03-render-output/maps/
    scan --render maps
    ```

    ```zsh
    # Charts for a specific task — writes HTML to tasks/{name}/charts/index.html
    scan --render charts elevation
    ```
    To generate a compiled interactive quarto document and HTML of all tasks, run:

    ```zsh
    scan --render scan-calculations
    ```
